findings.title: Duplicate junit and hamcrest test dependencies
findings.body: The diff adds junit and hamcrest test dependencies at lines 61-71, but these dependencies already exist earlier in the file (visible in the full content at the same coordinates). Maven allows duplicate dependency declarations but it is a defect: it produces a confusing POM, may trigger Maven warnings on some versions, and makes future maintenance error-prone (e.g., changing scope in one place but not the other). The added junit/hamcrest block should be removed since the dependencies are already declared.

findings.title: Dead code: discarded ASN1Encoder writes in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.body: In the anonymous ECDSACryptoProvider implementation, the two statements `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` (lines 114-115) create new ASN1Encoder instances, write a full INTEGER TLV into their internal ByteArrayOutputStream, and then discard the result. The actual DER sequence is built immediately after by the four chained `ASN1Encoder.create().write(...)` calls inside `writeDerSeq`. The discarded writes are wasted allocations and I/O and should be deleted to avoid misleading readers into thinking they are part of the encoding.

findings.title: logger.debugf called with a non-format string, will throw on class names containing %
findings.body: `logger.debugf(builder.toString())` passes a runtime-built string as the format argument. JBoss Logger's `debugf(String, Object...)` interprets the first argument as a `printf`-style format and expects additional varargs matching any `%` specifiers. If any class name returned by `ServiceLoader` contains a `%` (legal in JVM class names), `MissingFormatArgumentException` or similar will be thrown every time more than one provider is found, surfacing as an unexpected stack trace at debug level and, depending on JUL/LogManager configuration, potentially being promoted to a higher level. Use `logger.debug(builder.toString())` or `logger.debugf("%s", builder.toString())` instead.

findings.title: Most CryptoProvider methods throw UnsupportedOperationException; authz-client standalone usage is broken
findings.body: `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` is registered as the SPI provider for `org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider` in `authz/client/src/main/resources/META-INF/services/...`. However, nearly every method on the interface (`getAlgorithmProvider`, `getCertificateUtils`, `getPemUtils`, `getOCSPProver`, `getIdentityExtractorProvider`, `getEcdsaCryptoProvider().getPublicFromPrivate`, `createECParams`, `getKeyPairGen`, `getKeyFactory`, `getAesCbcCipher`, `getAesGcmCipher`, `getSecretKeyFact`, `getX509CertFactory`, `getCertStore`, `getCertPathBuilder`, `getSignature`, `wrapFactoryForTruststore`) is implemented as `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported yet.")`. The authz-client uses these facilities (notably `getSignature`, `getCertificateUtils`, `getPemUtils`, `getKeyPairGen`/`getKeyFactory`) when authenticating with signed-JWT client credentials and when parsing keys/certificates. When this module is used standalone (the documented intent), any such operation will throw UnsupportedOperationException at runtime, breaking client credential flows that involve private-key JWT, mutual TLS, or PEM key material. The PR should either implement these methods or document explicitly that the authz-client only supports the subset used for ECDSA R/S <-> DER conversion and fail fast at init time otherwise.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the JCE default provider, not BouncyCastle
findings.body: `getBouncyCastleProvider()` is implemented as `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`. This returns whatever JCE provider supplies the default keystore type on the host JVM (typically SUN/SunPKCS11/SunJSSE), not BouncyCastle. Callers that explicitly rely on a BC provider (e.g. to ask BC for algorithms/curves not present in the SUN provider) will silently get the SUN provider instead and may fail with `NoSuchAlgorithmException` later. Either return an actual BouncyCastleProvider (as `DefaultCryptoProvider` does) or, if BC is intentionally not bundled in the authz-client, throw UnsupportedOperationException so the failure mode is obvious.

findings.title: readSequence silently returns empty list for indefinite-length sequences and does not check for end-of-contents
findings.body: `readSequence` reads a length and then loops `while (length > 0)`. When `readLength()` returns `-1` for indefinite-length encoding (length byte `0x80`), the loop never executes and the method returns an empty `ArrayList`. The caller in `AuthzClientCryptoProvider.asn1derToConcatenatedRS` then fails with the misleading error "Invalid sequence with size different to 2". While DER (X.690 §10.1) forbids indefinite lengths for sequences, accepting BER signatures that use them would require consuming elements until the end-of-contents octets `0x00 0x00`. As written, any non-DER BER-encoded signature coming from another library will produce a confusing error rather than a clear one.

findings.title: Test only covers DER -> concat -> DER -> concat, not the inverse and not the values themselves
findings.body: The `test(ECDSAAlgorithm)` helper signs data with the JCE provider (DER output), converts to concatenated R/S, then back to DER and back to R/S, asserting the two concatenated forms are equal. It never verifies (a) the direct concatenatedRSToASN1DER round-trip with a known concatenated input, (b) that the produced DER bytes decode to the same BigInteger r,s values produced by the JCE Signature, and (c) that the produced concatenated bytes, when fed back into `Signature.verify` via `Signature.getInstance("NONEwithECDSA")` with the same algorithm, actually verify. Without (c) the test cannot catch sign-magnitude vs. two's-complement bugs, leading-zero handling bugs, or off-by-one in the `arraySize = len + 1` shift (which always prepends a 0 byte and can produce non-minimal DER).
